speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Prime Minister in view of the rising global interest rate outlook (a) what are the risks to the household debt situation in Singapore; (b) what is the proportion of mortgages accounting for household debt over the past five years; and (c) what measures are in place to reduce the build-up of highly-leveraged households and the associated vulnerabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Prime Minister in view of the short-term interest rates raised by the US Federal Reserve (a) what is the impact on mortgage rates in Singapore; (b) whether there has been an increase in mortgage delinquency; and (c) what are the plans to educate younger and first-time home buyers on expected higher borrowing costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is well within the TDSR threshold of 55%, which was tightened last year as part of the Government and MAS’ property cooling measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Third, household net wealth grew even through the pandemic, with household assets growing faster than household debt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Households’ liquid assets, such as cash and bank deposits, continued to exceed their total liabilities in aggregate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Most households should still be able to service their mortgages as Singapore’s domestic interest rates pick up alongside global rates from their current lows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, there will be a small segment of households with higher leverage, who will be more constrained by interest rate rises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: More broadly, all borrowers should exercise caution in their home purchases, to avoid having to cut back on other household expenditures if interest rates rise sharply.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The financial resilience of households to service their mortgages reflects the effects of measures that MAS has put in place over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This rate is about two percentage points higher than prevailing interest rates for new private property loans, which builds in a buffer for borrowers to service their mortgages across a normal interest rate cycle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Loan-to-value limits and restrictions on loan tenure have also encouraged greater financial prudence among mortgage borrowers of different profiles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, loan tenure restriction limits the duration and, hence, the overall financing that older borrowers can take up, because it is likely that income sources to support mortgage repayment would be more constrained after retirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS also requires that financial institutions (FIs) provide homebuyers with the information they need to make sound and prudent decisions, before extending them residential mortgages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This includes projections on how a borrower’s monthly mortgage instalments would vary under different interest rate scenarios.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MoneySense, our national financial education programme, also alerts consumers to important financial considerations when committing to a property purchase, including the recurrent, long-term costs involved.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan, you are taking both Question Nos 17 and 18 together, would that be correct?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, it is in regard to what the Minister of State mentioned just now about debt servicing being in good condition.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But, Mr Speaker, may I ask what is the proportion of the segment of those exposed in the population in terms of personal, unsecured loans?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second supplementary question is in regard to the domestic interest rate outlook.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Federal Reserve Bank of the US is expected to raise their rates quite significantly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The expectations are based on the committee's announcements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There will be sharp rate hikes over the course of the year and into 2023.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Given that it would definitely affect the domestic rate situation in Singapore and it would be very fast, it would definitely affect households and businesses in terms of cash outlays, especially so in the current inflation environment that we are seeing now.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister of State share what is our domestic rate outlook?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I think he mentioned about the projections and scenarios, but what does it mean for households and businesses, in terms of the rapid pace?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As the hon Member would know, the outlook for Singapore's domestic interest rates is closely tied to global rates.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Most Singapore-listed firms continue to hold sufficient liquidity in Q4 2021, with liquid assets, such as cash and cash equivalents, continuing to exceed their shorter-term liabilities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The debt servicing of Singapore-listed firms remains manageable, with most firms having sufficient earnings to cover their interest expenses, even in prescribed stressed scenarios of further increases in interest rates, with cash reserves providing additional buffers in this regard.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That said, the highly-leveraged companies, especially those with lower net profit margins, may find the increase in borrowing cost eroding their cashflow.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This would also apply to some of the SMEs which continue to underperform due to COVID-19 restrictions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But the broader economic recovery should provide some reprieve as Singapore opens up and emerges from the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To the Member's questions about personal unsecured lending, credit quality has remained generally favourable and stable over the past year, having improved from pre-pandemic levels.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Similarly, rollover balances as a share of GDP have inched down from 1.3% in Q4 2019, to 1% in Q4 2021.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In this regard, we urge consumers to be prudent with their new borrowings to reduce vulnerability to further income shocks and the higher interest rate environment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I would also like to assure the Member that MAS has also helped consumers who need assistance with their outstanding debt.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, consumers in financial distress can seek help from Credit Counselling Singapore for debt management assistance or by taking up commercial products such as debt consolidation plans that may alleviate their repayment burden.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think it is a very important question with regard to, particularly, first-time home buyers entering the property market at this juncture where potential interest rates can rise.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We also note that even as interest rates increase after an extended period when it was uncharacteristically low – we had that whole period where interest rates were just uncharacteristically low over time – household income, as I had mentioned in my original answer, is expected to continue to grow alongside the broader economic recovery as we emerge from the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Second, the Member would be pleased to know that MoneySense educates the public on property loan issues through a property resource guide on its website and social media posts, where issues covered include the importance of buying within one's means and the features of different types of loans.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MoneySense intends to push out more material on the impact of rising interest rates on financial decisions, including on property purchases.
